what_this_is: The paper.pdf that commit d1a7c63 shipped, retained under its own name after paper/paper.pdf was recompiled on 2026-09-24.
why_retained: docs/operations-log.md quotes that digest as the output of the 173-claim delivery chain, and scripts/verify_paper_claims.py enforces that every 64-hex string quoted in the docs is a real digest of something on disk. Recompiling paper/paper.pdf would have left the log quoting a hash with no referent, so the gate would have gone red -- or, worse, been loosened. Keeping the bytes is the option that leaves both the history and the gate intact. The digest is also recoverable from git (git show d1a7c63:paper/paper.pdf), but the gate scans the working tree, not the object store.

the_build_it_came_from.hashes_taken_from: git show d1a7c63:<path> | sha256sum, i.e. the committed blob bytes, not this working tree
the_build_it_came_from.freshness_gate_at_that_commit: mtime-based, and therefore not reproducible from a clone. That is the defect that produced this file: see paper/BUILD_PIN.json and the 'second correction' paragraph in paper/paper.tex.

not_the_current_submission: paper/paper.pdf is current. This copy is a referent for a quoted digest and a record of what the 173-claim chain certified.
